title: Tubuloside A attenuates sepsis-induced acute lung injury by modulating the NF-kappaB p50-Nrf2/GPX4 axis to suppress inflammation, oxidative stress and ferroptosis.
authors: Guan, Tianyue; Dela, Audrey; Jin, Yichen; Song, Juqin; Wang, Tingyan; Zhu, Yu; Dong, Jingquan; Zhao, Panpan
one_liner_zh: 研究药物Tubuloside A通过NF-kappaB p50-Nrf2/GPX4轴减轻脓毒症肺损伤，涉及分子对接预测蛋白-小分子结合，但核心是疾病治疗机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法上仅简单对接，无AI或MD深度建模。
abstract: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI) remains a critical factor contributing to mortality in intensive care units, and effective therapeutic strategies are still lacking. The present research explores the defensive impacts and associated mechanisms of Tubuloside A (TA), an active phenanthrenoid glycoside extracted from Cistanche deserticola, in sepsis-induced ALI. Utilizing both a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse model and LPS-stimulated MLE-12 alveolar epithelial cells, we found that TA markedly attenuated lung injury, as indicated by improved histopathological features, reduced pulmonary edema, and maintenance of alveolar structure. Mechanistically, TA provided multifaceted protection by concurrently inhibiting oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling-critical drivers of sepsis-induced ALI. Treatment with TA diminished lipid peroxidation, restored GPX4 expression, and inhibited pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta). Network pharmacology identified NFKB1 as a therapeutic target of TA against ALI. Molecular docking predicted and SPR analysis verified that TA binds to NF-kappaB p50. Notably, functional validation via NF-kappaB p50 overexpression abolished TA-mediated protection and re-sensitized cells to ferroptosis, confirming NF-kappaB p50 as a central regulatory node. Furthermore, TA activated Nrf2 signaling in an NF-kappaBp50-dependent manner, as demonstrated by nuclear translocation assays and rescue experiments. Calcein AM imaging and iron chelation studies confirmed that TA's anti-ferroptotic effect requires functional NF-kappaB/Nrf2/GPX4 crosstalk. Collectively, our findings reveal that TA ameliorates sepsis-ALI by targeting the NF-kappaBp50-Nrf2/GPX4 axis to coordinately inhibit inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis, highlighting its potential as a multi-target phytotherapeutic agent for acute respiratory disorders.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症诱导的急性肺损伤（ALI）仍是重症监护病房中导致死亡的关键因素，且目前缺乏有效的治疗策略。本研究探讨了管花肉苁蓉中提取的活性苯丙素苷类化合物管花苷A（Tubuloside A, TA）在脓毒症诱导的ALI中的保护作用及其相关机制。通过使用盲肠结扎穿刺（CLP）小鼠模型和LPS刺激的MLE-12肺泡上皮细胞，我们发现TA显著减轻了肺损伤，表现为组织病理学特征改善、肺水肿减少以及肺泡结构维持。机制上，TA通过同时抑制氧化应激、铁死亡（ferroptosis）和炎症信号——这些是脓毒症诱导ALI的关键驱动因素——提供了多方面的保护。TA处理降低了脂质过氧化，恢复了GPX4表达，并抑制了促炎细胞因子（TNF-alpha、IL-6、IL-1beta）。网络药理学鉴定出NFKB1为TA抗ALI的治疗靶点。分子对接预测和表面等离子体共振（SPR）分析验证了TA与NF-kappaB p50的结合。值得注意的是，通过NF-kappaB p50过表达进行的功能验证消除了TA介导的保护作用，并使细胞重新对铁死亡敏感，确认NF-kappaB p50是核心调控节点。此外，TA以NF-kappaB p50依赖性方式激活Nrf2信号，这通过核转位实验和救援实验得到证实。Calcein AM成像和铁螯合研究确认，TA的抗铁死亡效应需要功能性NF-kappaB/Nrf2/GPX4串扰。总体而言，我们的发现揭示TA通过靶向NF-kappaB p50-Nrf2/GPX4轴，协同抑制炎症、氧化应激和铁死亡，从而改善脓毒症诱导的ALI，凸显其作为急性呼吸系统疾病多靶点植物治疗剂的潜力。
